tasks.short: Research community needs and program goals

steps.what: Gather member and community needs notes
Count the needs notes by theme
Draft program directions from the needs rows

loop.input: need rows and the direction template
loop.output: directions that cite need ids only
loop.check: Every direction cites a need id on the list
loop.stop: One pass; drop any direction with no need id
loop.why_not_simpler: Choosing a goal is not a sort of the counts

steps.what: Analyze needs and determine program goals
File the signed needs direction

tasks.design: Need notes land in {SPREADSHEET} with need id, area, program id and source. Counts by theme are a filter, not a judgement. A bounded note in {DOCS} proposes directions that cite need ids. The manager analyzes the needs, signs the goals, and only that note is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs were anecdotes in meetings, so a draft could not show which note a direction relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: A need id can be stored with the note, so a count and a citation can use the same row.
tasks.still_hard: Which need becomes a program goal is a choice about the community, not a sort order.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the program directions and goals. The count does not rank people.

ambition.what: Revisit program goals when new needs rows arrive, not only in a yearly plan

tasks.altitude: Less time recounting anecdotes. The manager can refuse a direction that cites no need row.

reach.task: Confirm program goals against the signed needs note
reach.learn: Which goals cite a need row and which are still open

evidence.claim: Researching community needs is a mix of notes and a judgement about goals. Counting rows is the small part. Choosing the goal is not.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. A needs direction is checked by a person against the source rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends at a signed needs direction. Funding the new goal is a later budget task.
Input contract: need id, area, program id, source name, period, count. Producer is the manager or a colleague who heard the need. A note with no need id is not counted.
Meetings remain for the goal decision. Use the spreadsheet's own filters before custom code. The count does not score members.
unknowns: Whether members will accept their comments being stored as need rows.
research_questions: What share of need notes has no area or program id?
How often does the signed goal differ from the draft direction?

already_counted.description: Manager edits directions that cite a weak row
Goal decision time stays in the review

incremental.description: Add a theme when members raise a need the list does not name

approvals.approved_version: needs direction signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes needs stay as meeting anecdotes, so the count is thin and the manager still gathers by hand. The high case assumes rows are clean but every goal decision and the sign-off stay manual. The discussion of goals is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Draft the community training programs outline

loop.input: approved manual paragraphs and the outline template
loop.output: an outline that cites paragraph ids
loop.check: Every section cites a paragraph id from the signed manual
loop.stop: One pass; leave a blank where a paragraph id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: How to teach a room is not in the paragraph store

steps.what: Sign the training programs plan
Place the signed dates on the calendar
Implement the training programs with volunteer
Evaluate the training programs after the session

tasks.design: A bounded outline in {DOCS} uses only paragraphs from the signed manual. The manager signs the training plan, including dates and program id. Those dates are placed on the {CALENDAR}. The manager implements the session and later evaluates it. Attendance is a list the manager already keeps in {HCM}, not a score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlines were rewritten from old manuals, and dates lived in mail, so a session could not be tied to a signed plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Approved manual paragraphs and a plan id can be reused, so an outline can cite them and a calendar entry can use the signed dates only.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching the room, and judging whether the program worked, still depends on the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager signs the plan, runs the session and evaluates the program. Dates are not assigned by a roster solver.

ambition.what: Evaluate each training program after the session, not only at year end

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting the outline. The session and the evaluation stay. The manager can refuse a date that was not on the signed plan.

reach.task: Attend the session on the signed date
reach.learn: Which training plan is current and which evaluation is still open

evidence.claim: Running a training program is a session in a room. The outline can be prepared. The teaching and the evaluation cannot.
Digest [S7] describes document drafting from approved text where a person still checks. The outline uses signed manual paragraphs and the manager still signs the plan.
Digest [S12] says a Dutch works council is consulted under article 27 before a system that schedules staff. This step places dates the manager already signed and is not a roster solver.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task runs from a signed plan through the session and the evaluation. Building a shift roster is out of scope.
Input contract: plan id, program id, paragraph id, date, room, audience. Producer is the manager from the signed manual. A paragraph with no id is not copied into the outline.
The meeting prior fits the session. Use the calendar's own entries before custom code. If attendance is later used to judge staff, consult the works council first.
unknowns: Whether a works council must see training dates before they are placed.
Who evaluates a session the manager did not teach.
research_questions: What share of outline pages has no approved paragraph?
How often is a session evaluated more than a month late?

already_counted.description: Manager edits the outline before signing the plan
Session time stays with the manager

incremental.description: Add outline sections when a training program changes

approvals.approved_version: training plan signed for this program id
training evaluation signed after this session

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes manuals are not split into approved paragraphs, so the outline is still written by hand. The high case assumes the outline drafts cleanly but the session, the sign-off and the evaluation stay manual. Teaching time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Ask how regulations and policies apply
Retrieve the regulations and policies passages

loop.input: the question and the policy file
loop.output: passage ids that match the topic
loop.check: Every returned item has a passage id that exists in the file
loop.stop: One pass; return an empty list if none match
loop.why_not_simpler: A question's wording does not equal a passage by a fixed table

steps.what: Draft an interpretation from those passages

loop.output: a note in which each sentence cites a passage id
loop.check: Every sentence cites a passage id on the list and names no person as eligible
loop.stop: One pass; drop any sentence with no passage id
loop.why_not_simpler: The meaning where two texts meet is not a copy of one passage

steps.what: Sign the interpretation for agency staff
Explain the signed interpretation in the meeting
File the signed interpretation note

tasks.design: Agency staff ask a question with program id and topic by {EMAIL}. Passages are retrieved from {DOCS} by policy id. A bounded note drafts an interpretation that quotes only those passages. The manager signs it, explains it, and the file stores the signed note. The note does not decide a person's eligibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers were given from memory in calls, so the same regulation could be explained two ways and neither way cited the text.
tasks.enabler_now: Policy id and passage id can be stored with the text, so an answer can be limited to passages that exist.
tasks.still_hard: What a regulation means for this program is still a judgement, especially where two texts meet.
tasks.human_edge: The manager interprets the regulations and policies. The note is advice, not a decision about a person.

ambition.what: File a checked interpretation when the same regulation question has been asked twice

tasks.altitude: Less time searching for the passage. The explanation stays a conversation. The manager can refuse an answer that cites no passage.

reach.task: Apply the signed interpretation in their own program
reach.learn: Which passage was cited and that the note does not decide a person

evidence.claim: Interpreting regulations is advice from texts plus a conversation. A retrieved passage can support the advice. It does not replace the manager.
Digest [S1] describes policy-library management that versions policy texts and can summarise regulatory documents for a person to review.
Digest [S2] describes a European governance, risk and compliance register used for policy and control tasks, including regulatory material. It is not a measured result for this team.
Digest [S9] on GDPR article 22 requires a person to decide eligibility. This interpretation is advice and is not a solely automated decision about a person.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. The interpretation is checked against the passage rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends at a signed interpretation explained to agency staff. Deciding one person's eligibility is out of scope.
Input contract: question id, program id, policy id, passage id, topic. Producer of the question is agency staff. Producer of the passage is the policy file. A sentence with no passage id is dropped.
The answer-desk shape fits the draft. The meeting prior still fits the explanation. Use the document store's own search before custom code.
unknowns: Whether county texts are in the same store as the internal policies.
Who may sign an interpretation when the manager is away.
research_questions: What share of questions has no matching policy id?
How often does the manager change the drafted interpretation?

already_counted.description: Manager edits the interpretation before signing
Explanation time stays in the meeting

incremental.description: Add a passage id when a regulation text changes

approvals.approved_version: interpretation signed for this question id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes regulations are not split into passages, so retrieval fails and the manager still reads from paper. The high case assumes passages exist but every interpretation is still signed and explained by the manager. The conversation is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Draft talking points on programs and policies

loop.input: signed policy rows and the points template
loop.output: points that cite a policy id
loop.check: Every point cites a policy id on the signed rows
loop.stop: One pass; drop any point with no policy id
loop.why_not_simpler: How to say a point to a particular group is not a field

steps.what: Sign the community talking points
Speak to community groups about programs
File the talking points that were used

tasks.design: Talking points in {DOCS} are drafted only from signed policy rows: program id, purpose and policy id. The manager signs that text. The talk to the community group stays in the room, on the {CALENDAR}. Only the signed points are filed afterwards. {EMAIL} is not used to send an unsigned draft.
tasks.previous_blocker: Talking points were rewritten the night before from memory, so a public line could drift from the signed policy.
tasks.enabler_now: Purpose and policy id can be read from the signed file, so a point can cite them or be dropped.
tasks.still_hard: Speaking to a group, and answering what they ask, is the work.
tasks.human_edge: The manager speaks and decides what to say when a question leaves the signed points.
tasks.altitude: The talk stays almost the whole task. The manager can refuse a point that is not in the signed policies.

reach.task: Hear the programs and policies as signed
reach.learn: Which points were signed and which questions were left open

evidence.claim: Speaking to a community group is almost entirely in the room. Only the talking points can be prepared, and only from text already signed.
Digest [S7] describes document drafting from approved text where a person still checks. The manager signs the points before the talk.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. Public points are checked against the policy rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends after the talk and the filing of the points that were used. Media interviews are a different task.
Input contract: program id, purpose text, policy id, audience, date. Producer is the signed policy file. A point with no policy id is dropped, not invented.
The meeting prior fits and is accepted. Almost all remaining time is the talk. Use the document store's own template before custom code.
unknowns: Which community groups want the points in advance.
Who speaks when the manager cannot attend.
research_questions: What share of talks uses points that cite a policy id?
How often does a question fall outside the signed points?

already_counted.description: Manager edits points before the talk
Speaking time stays in the room

incremental.description: Update the points template when a program purpose changes

approvals.approved_version: talking points signed for this audience and date

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes policies are not in citable rows, so the points are still written by hand before the talk. The high case assumes the draft is clean but the sign-off and the talk stay with the manager. Speaking time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Needs notes and regulation answers are drafted from source rows. Training sessions and community talks stay in the room with the manager.
reach: Agency staff receive an interpretation note that cites the policy passage, after the manager has checked it.
Community groups hear talking points the manager has signed, not an unchecked draft.
skills_to_grow: Tie a needs finding to a counted row before choosing a program goal.
Answer a regulation question from the policy text, not from memory alone.
Keep a community talk inside the signed purposes and policies.
role.ambitious_version: Each program direction cites a needs row, and each regulation answer cites a policy passage the manager has signed.
